newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols keep bulk of hefty gains.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark vols keep bulk of hefty gains.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/pair options kept the bulk of sharp gains Monday as the dollar perched near new multi-year highs versus the mark.

But the dollar's surge slowed and options business ebbed as the unit ground up to 1.7992 marks Monday afternoon in a move analysts characterized as stemming more from mark weakness than dollar strength.

The dollar's flirtation with 1.80 marks, which also kept traders guessing about potential for central bank intervention to support the mark, pumped up front-end dollar/mark vols more than 1.75 percentage points from late Friday's levels.
"They're (vols) quite a bit higher," said a bank broker. "This overshot most...expectations of the dollar rally."
"It's been very quiet during our day, but things definitely moved a lot overnight," said John Bird, senior currency options analyst, Technical Data Corp.
After midday Monday, one-month dollar/mark stood at about 10.4/10.7 percent, up from 9.9/10.2 earlier Monday and compared to 8.3/8.6 pct at Friday's close.
"I think it's mainly people are just trying to buy volatility in general by just paying the at-the-moneys across the board, bidding them up," said the broker of dollar/mark.

"The thing is, I think people are waiting to buy upper strikes just because the vols are so expensive and the skew is so great now," he added. "So I think they're probably just hoping to bid them in or wait for a little bit of a pullback before they start buying too aggressively on the upside."
Uncertainty over whether a rise to 1.80 marks might spark intervention also underpinned the dollar/mark risk reversal.
Bird quoted the one-month, 25-delta reversal at 0.3/0.6 points, favoring mark puts, versus 0.0/0.3 points Friday.
"That (risk reversal) started getting bid up last week," Bird said. "It's been creeping up over a period of days."
The options broker noted an even steeper skew toward mark puts, at 0.65/0.95 points versus 0.5/0.7 at Monday's open.
Front-end dollar/yen vols held firm near 9.9/10.2 percent versus 9.3/9.6 percent late Friday, with players seen testing vols because spot has stayed stuck.
Dollar/yen drew couple of large deals Monday, one done overnight in Asia involving sale of $600 million of one-month at-the-money straddles at about 9.35 percent, brokers said.
Another involved purchase of $750 million of deep out-of-the-money one-year dollar/yen calls, a deal the bank broker said "was paid up quite a bit" from 10.4 to 10.7 percent.
Dollar/yen risk-reversal was quoted at 1.6/1.9 points Monday, up from 1.4 points given last Friday but still sharply below the peak near 3.0 points given early last week.
"Everyone thought we were going to have a sharp move to the downside in dollar/yen, and now people pretty much don't think that's going to be the case any longer," Bird said.
Sterling stayed strong versus the mark on interest rate differentials, but spot attracted more attention than options.
"I think it's just been such a one-way move that it's been easier for people to play it on a spot basis," Bird added. ((Derivatives Desk (312) 408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
